scope: Nonlinear1D Lagrangian prototype using graph-reconstructed cooling, not a certified reproduction of Figures3–6

cold_extension.form: Continuous CII-like low-T asymptote: electron factor T^-1/2 and neutral factor T^0, both exp(-92/T), anchored at the lowest source temperature. Not recovered historical input.

limitations: Cooling uses51 digitized Figure1 points;12 warm-end points were added for the locally hotter part of an initially isobaric density wave. Linear input and results are preserved.
No hard temperature floor or density clipping. Below the graph domain a declared CII-like asymptote is used; every exposure is recorded and an alternate asymptote is compared.
For x below.001, the two lowest source-x curves are continued linearly to a nonnegative neutral-collider contribution. This is a declared extrapolation, not a recovered rate.
The published coordinate is zone number; the original mass/grid mapping is not fully specified. Our plots use equal-H-mass coordinate and also export physical positions.

An explicit compatible midpoint pressure-work step uses compression-only artificial viscosity. Conduction is conservative semi-implicit backward Euler and thus limits temporal order; a half-timestep comparison is required.
Initial density is a sinusoid in physical position, initially isobaric, with zero velocity and uniform ionization. The mean unperturbed temperature is8200K; local initial temperatures vary.
No external heating, continued ionization, magnetic pressure, gravity, thermal H ionization, or He ionization. Recombination uses the same declared historical H approximation as the linear prototype.
Convergence checks assess this implementation; agreement with the1972 nonlinear cloud parameters is measured separately and not assumed.
The historical-scale mesh study is not a continuum-converged resolution claim. The Field-length proxy criterion and fixed-time profile differences are diagnostic results, even when unmet.
artificial_viscosity: Compression-only quadratic plus linear vonNeumann-style pressure, included in compatible pressure work; no physical viscosity is claimed.
comparison_note: Historical-mesh study at64/96/128equal-mass cells, plus an auxiliary512-cell run. The source reports100–200points; sub100runs are exploratory, not asserted original settings. Continuum/front-resolution criteria are reported separately and may remain unmet.
